key_insight: Accurate animal identification does not necessarily mean a model recognizes the animal itself. Counterfactual Foreground Retrieval (CFR) evaluates the evidence behind a match, aiming to distinguish animal-based recognition from identity-correlated shortcuts.
problem_solved: Standard retrieval accuracy leaves unclear whether models use identifying animal features or incidental cues correlated with identity, limiting confidence in benchmark results.
method: Introduce CFR as an evidence-aware evaluation protocol for individual animal identification.
Evaluate the same query–gallery retrieval task through a counterfactual lens to investigate what supports identity matches.
Focus evaluation on animal-feature evidence versus identity-correlated shortcuts; the provided abstract is truncated before the experimental details.
impact: CFR could help practitioners assess whether strong retrieval scores reflect meaningful animal recognition. This supports more informed evaluation of shared benchmarks and reusable foundation models.

paper_title: CounterFactual Retrieval for Evidence-Aware Individual Animal Identification
paper_authors: Ankit K. Upadhyay, Aleksandr Algasov, Ekaterina Nepovinnykh, Fedor Zolotarev, Tuomas Eerola
